newsitem.title: USA: NYS local, state issuers set bond sales for Q3.
newsitem.headline: NYS local, state issuers set bond sales for Q3.

text.p: New York State's Controller said Monday that state and local issuers proposed selling $3.158 billion of bonds in the third quarter, including a debut sale by a new New York City agency.

New York City Transitional Finance Authority, approved by Albany early this year to help the city circumvent its debt cap, plans to sell $600 million of bonds in September, said the state controller, H. Carl McCall, in prepared remarks.

McCall, who chairs the state committee that coordinates sales, noted the schedule will be modified as program needs and market conditions change. And the sales can only go forward if all projects are approved as required by law.
The following list details the bond sales planned.
--New York City, $800 million July bond sale.
--Thruway Authority, $360 million sale in July, and $325 million in August.

--Dormitory Authority, July bond sales of $10.2 million, $6 million, $32.1 million, $11.2 million. August bond sales of $5 million, $170 million, $52 million. September bond sales of $28 million, $150 million, and $19 million.
--Metropolitan Transportation Authority, $400 million bond sale in September.
--Empire State Development Corp/Job Development Authority, $27 million in September.
--Housing Finance Agency, September bond sales of $91 million and $72 million.

Entities weighing refunding sales include: New York State, New York City, the New York City Housing Development Corp, the Municipal Assistance Corp for the City of New York, the State of New York Mortgage Agency, the Environmental Facilities Corp, the Energy Research and Development Authority, the Metropolitan Transportation Authority, the State of New York Mortgage Agency and the Dormitory Authority.

McCall added no public sales now were being considered by the state, the Local Government Assistance Corp, the Triborough Bridge and Tunnel Authority, the Power Authority, or the Battery Park City Authority.
